# Takahiro Miki

> Takahiro Miki, research scientist at Google DeepMind working on Gemini Robotics. PhD from ETH Zurich on perceptive legged locomotion; DARPA SubT winner with Team CERBERUS.

## Projects

- Gemini Robotics 2 (2025–now): One model for any robot body, from tabletop arms to full humanoids.
- Learning perceptive locomotion (2019–2025): Reinforcement learning that lets legged robots see the ground and still trust their legs.
- Safe and robust learned control (2023–2026): Finding where learned controllers fail, and teaching them to be careful.
- Natural motion: animal priors and humanoids (2025–2026): Learning from recorded motion so robots move naturally, then adapting it to rough terrain.
- Elevation mapping and navigation (2021–2023): elevation_mapping_cupy: fast, GPU-based terrain maps for legged robots, and planning on top of them.
- Legged manipulation (2021–2024): Legs that also handle things: opening doors, balancing an arm, catching a ball.
- DARPA Subterranean Challenge (2019–2021): First place and the $2,000,000 prize in the 2021 Final.
- Science in the field (2023–2026): Taking legged robots to volcanoes, planetary analog sites and city streets.
- Early work: drones, rovers and teams (2015–2020): Where it started: aerial robots, lunar rovers and multi-robot decision-making.
- Side quest: LLM security (2024): Hiding a secret inside a language model, and trying to steal everyone else’s.
